contract:
New migration; renumber if another area claims this timestamp. The header documents the LIVE STATE above (columns, relacl authenticated=arwdDxtm / anon=arwdDxtm, posts_update_own, both triggers, edit_metadata = clip overlays, not reused) and the SECURITY GAP it closes (see hazards: created_at, tags, view_count and media_url can be written directly through PostgREST today, and media_url swaps are signed by /api/posts/[id]/media).

SQL:
1) `alter table public.posts add column if not exists edited_at timestamptz;` with no backfill. NULL means never edited.
2) `create or replace function public.posts_stamp_edited() returns trigger language plpgsql set search_path = public as $$ begin if old.status = 'published' and new.content is distinct from old.content then new.edited_at := now(); else new.edited_at := old.edited_at; end if; return new; end $$;` NOT security definer. It always overwrites the client's value, so edited_at can never be set or cleared by a client. Edits to a draft, and the draft-to-published flip, do not stamp.
3) `create trigger posts_stamp_edited before update on public.posts for each row execute function public.posts_stamp_edited();` It fires after posts_stamp_campus alphabetically and touches no campus columns. The campuses-rename cascade at depth 2 does not change content, so it keeps the old value.
4) `revoke update on public.posts from anon, authenticated; grant update (content, tags, status) on public.posts to authenticated;` This keeps the one user-client writer working (route.ts:356-363 writes content/status, and E1 adds tags). record_post_view and bump_org_activity_from_post are SECURITY DEFINER, and FK cascades run as the owner, so they are unaffected.
5) `notify pgrst, 'reload schema';`

PRE-CHECK comment, read-only, all must pass: `rg -n 'from\("posts"\)' src` shows .update only at src/app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts:358 and no .upsert on posts. `rg -n "from\('posts'\)|rest/v1/posts" public/html src/lib` shows no writers (src/lib/metrics/post-audience.ts:124 is a read).

POST-CHECK queries in a comment: has_column_privilege('authenticated','public.posts',c,'UPDATE') is true for content, tags, status and false for id, user_id, org_id, type, media_url, media_thumbnail_url, created_at, view_count, edit_metadata, campus_id, school_system, edited_at. The same check for anon is false for every column. The pg_trigger row posts_stamp_edited exists. The information_schema.columns row posts.edited_at exists.

Apply through the management API with curl, plus a schema_migrations row (security model memory). Apply BEFORE any batch that selects edited_at is pushed. It is safe to apply now: HEAD code writes only content/status with the user client.
acceptance: The post-check query returns exactly: authenticated UPDATE true for content, tags and status only; anon false everywhere.
Read-only probe after apply: `select tgname from pg_trigger where tgname='posts_stamp_edited'` returns 1 row, and posts.edited_at exists and is NULL on all 21 rows.
Existing publish, delete, view-count and feed flows still work: record_post_view is SECURITY DEFINER; spot-check /api/posts/<id>/view on localhost signed in.
No other migration in the same wave touches posts grants.
